body_en: Brussels Airport to cancel all flights on Monday due to national strike - Aviation24.be
Home Airports Brussels Airport (BRU) Brussels Airport to cancel all flights on Monday due to national strike

Brussels Airport will cancel all arriving and departing passenger flights on Monday, 23 November, following confirmation of disruption linked to the nationwide industrial action in Belgium. The disruption follows a national demonstration organised by Belgium’s main trade unions ACV-CSC, ABVV-FGTB and ACLVB, protesting against the federal government’s socio-economic and austerity measures.

According to information from Belgian air navigation service provider skeyes, the industrial action will have a major impact on air traffic operations. With air traffic control unable to guarantee normal operations, Brussels Airport is expected to suspend all scheduled passenger flight movements for the day between 7:00 and 21:00.

The cancellations will affect airlines operating at Belgium’s main international airport, including Brussels Airlines, TUI fly Belgium, Ryanair and several international carriers. Both arriving and departing passengers are expected to be affected.

Passengers scheduled to travel on Monday are advised not to travel to the airport without first checking directly with their airline. Airlines are expected to contact affected passengers regarding rebooking and alternative travel arrangements.
The industrial action is part of a nationwide protest against government policies, with significant disruption also expected on public transport networks across Belgium.
Further details regarding the exact number of cancelled flights and the impact on cargo operations are not yet available.

主页 机场 布鲁塞尔机场 (BRU) 由于全国罢工，布鲁塞尔机场周一取消所有航班
在确认与比利时全国罢工有关的中断后，布鲁塞尔机场将于 11 月 23 日星期一取消所有抵达和出发的客运航班。此前，比利时主要工会 ACV-CSC、ABVV-FGTB 和 ACLVB 组织了全国示威活动，抗议联邦政府的社会经济和紧缩措施。
据比利时空中导航服务提供商Skeyes消息，此次罢工将对空中交通运营产生重大影响。由于空中交通管制无法保证正常运行，布鲁塞尔机场预计将暂停当天7:00至21:00之间的所有定期客运航班起降。
取消航班将影响在比利时主要国际机场运营的航空公司，包括布鲁塞尔航空、比利时途易航空、瑞安航空和几家国际航空公司。预计抵达和出发的乘客都会受到影响。
建议计划周一出行的乘客在未直接咨询航空公司的情况下不要前往机场。航空公司预计将就重新预订和替代旅行安排事宜联系受影响的乘客。
此次罢工是全国范围内抗议政府政策的一部分，预计比利时各地的公共交通网络也会受到严重干扰。

title_en: Why Airlines Accept The Airbus A321XLR's Heavier 101.5-Tonne Maximum Takeoff Weight On Flights Shorter Than An Hour
title_zh: 为什么航空公司在短于一小时的航班上接受空客 A321XLR 较重的 101.5 吨最大起飞重量
summary: Airlines have ultimately deemed the weight penalty a necessary trade-off for the Airbus A321XLR.
summary_zh: 航空公司最终认为重量损失是空客 A321XLR 的必要权衡。
body_en: Based in the UK, Josh is a keen writer with a degree in Military History. Having worked previously as a financial journalist, he has covered the aviation industry extensively, reporting on airlines' results and monthly passenger statistics in the aftermath of the pandemic, alongside the likes of regulation around sustainable fuels, and the prospects for hydrogen-powered commercial flight. He joins Simple Flying with a lifelong love of all things aviation.

The Airbus A321XLR has helped open a new chapter in long-and-thin aviation. As the latest variant to appear in the Airbus A320 family, the XLR — or Extra Long Range — has taken the crown as the longest-range commercial narrowbody. Simply put, it has provided operators with arguably the best means yet of efficiently serving long-haul routes that would otherwise be unsuited to larger, widebody aircraft.

Despite its impressive capabilities, airlines have been known to put the XLR to work on connections that span a fraction of the distance the aircraft can actually fly. In some extreme cases, these do not even stretch to an hour of flight time. But modifications were needed for the XLR to earn its title, and these added weight. So for those opting to schedule their XLRs on such short routes, the reality is accepting the penalties of operating a heavier plane than might normally do the job. Nonetheless, carriers continue to do so anyway, which raises the question: Why?

On the surface, the A321XLR and standard Airbus A321neo appear almost identical . They share a score of common features, from their engines to their capacities to their basic dimensions, including wingspans and the same fuselage length, width, and height. A bystander could not be blamed for mistaking one for the other as a result.

Airbus deliberately developed the duo this way too, with these retained features making it operationally viable for airlines to operate both variants in their fleets. Unchanged dimensions mean the same gate spacing and ground equipment can be used at airports, for instance. It also simplifies crew training, as pilots can fly either variant without having to train for an entirely separate type rating.
Select A321XLR and A321neo specifications, from Airbus

There are key differences between the two, which is why the XLR has a stronger range and higher maximum takeoff weight . The range is largely enabled by the addition of a permanent 3,407.82-US gallon (12,900-3liter) rear center tank on the XLR, which also explains the increased weight; Airbus has also developed an updated fuel system and outfitted the variant with necessary structural reinforcements. Ultimately, this has pushed the XLR’s maximum range to 4,700 nautical miles (8,700 km) — which is a notable step up on the NEO’s .
But Several Airlines Schedule A321XLRs On Short Routes

Because of this, any instance where an airline chooses to use the A321XLR on a short-haul hop may seem counterintuitive. Indeed, the XLR was specifically designed to increase the A320 family's top range. Even so, many airlines do use the variant for this purpose in practice.

Air Canada uses its XLRs in part to connect Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (YOW) and Toronto Pearson International Airport (YYZ), as well as Montréal-Trudeau International Airport (YUL) and Toronto, for instance. Each of these journeys lasts roughly 39 and 53 minutes, respectively, spanning between 197 nautical miles (364 km) and 274 nautical miles (507 km). Concurrently, the carrier also services its almost nine-hour Toronto to Tenerife South Airport (TFS) route using XLRs.

Across the Atlantic, Ireland’s Aer Lingus XLRs flew more than 300 flights exceeding 3,100 miles (2,694 nautical miles or 4,989 km), alongside over 200 flights of 1,250 miles (1,086 nautical miles or 2,012 km) or fewer, in July this year, according to aviation data platform Avi-Go . These included Dublin Airport (DUB) to Nashville International Airport (BNA), scheduled at nine hours and 20 minutes, but also Dublin to London Heathrow Airport (LHR) and Dublin to Josep Tarradellas Barcelona–El Prat Airport (BCN), lasting just 48 minutes and one hour and 50 minutes, respectively. Needless to say, the XLR is by no means solely used for its range in either case.
A321XLR Deliveries Still In Their Early Stages

Air Canada and Aer Lingus are not alone, though. It is common practice among A321XLR operators to run the models on diverse routes with wide-ranging flight times and distances. At least, this is the case as it stands.

Based on data from aviation analyst Cirium covering last July, American Airlines, Saudia, and Wizz Air were among the handful of XLR operators that were doing just that. The former flew its XLRs on journeys spanning the 540- to 1,079-nautical mile (1,000- to 1,999-km) and 2,700 to 3,239-nautical mile (5,000- to 5,999-km) brackets, as well as everything in between. Interestingly, these figures showed Iberia — the XLR’s launch customer back in October 2024 — was the only carrier to exclusively use the variant for connections in the highest 2,700- to 3,239-nautical mile (5,000- to 5,999-km) and 3,240- to 3,779-nautical mile (6,000- to 6,999-km) brackets over the course of the month.

In other words, the carrier that has had the most time to incorporate the aircraft into its fleet appeared to be the one getting the most out of the XLR’s range most frequently. That is not surprising, though, given Airbus has only begun delivering the model in the past few years. By our count, just 61 models had been delivered to 11 carriers as of the time of writing in November, out of more than 500 orders placed.
Airlines Still Toying With A321XLR Schedules As A Result?

As such, those tasked with fitting the A321XLR into wider schedules have only recently benefited from the jets actually being on hand. Although orders placed years in advance will have given time to prepare, there is little replacement for real-world experience — especially since the XLR is, in many ways, unmatched by anything that has come before it.

In Iberia’s case, the XLR has appeared more capable than anticipated. “ [It’s] even better than originally planned in terms of stage length, ” chief executive Marco Antonio Trujillo said previously. “ In fact, we are operating currently to the Caribbean, San Juan and Santo Domingo, where initially we were not thinking that the range could get over there. ”

On the flip side, Air Canada had planned to introduce XLRs between Toronto and London Heathrow this year. However, the Canadian flag carrier pulled the type before it could even debut on the service, instead opting to stick with narrowbodies for the time being. All of this goes to say, planning in advance is one thing, but meeting operational requirements in real time can be another story altogether.
body_zh: 乔什居住在英国，是一位热心作家，拥有军事史学位。此前，他曾担任财经记者，广泛报道了航空业，报道了疫情后航空公司的业绩和每月乘客统计数据，以及可持续燃料的监管以及氢动力商业航班的前景等。他带着对航空一切事物的终生热爱加入了 Simple Flying。
空客 A321XLR 帮助开启了细长航空的新篇章。作为空中客车 A320 系列中的最新型号，XLR（即超长航程）已成为航程最长的商用窄体飞机。简而言之，它为运营商提供了可以说是迄今为止有效服务长途航线的最佳方式，否则这些航线不适合大型宽体飞机。
尽管其功能令人印象深刻，但众所周知，航空公司将 XLR 用于跨越飞机实际飞行距离一小部分的连接。在某些极端情况下，这些甚至不会延长到一个小时的飞行时间。但 XLR 需要进行一些修改才能赢得这一称号，而这些修改也增加了重量。因此，对于那些选择在如此短的航线上安排 XLR 飞机的人来说，现实是接受驾驶比正常情况下更重的飞机的惩罚。尽管如此，运营商仍然继续这样做，这就提出了一个问题：为什么？
从表面上看，A321XLR 和标准空客 A321neo 几乎完全相同。它们具有许多共同特征，从发动机到容量再到基本尺寸，包括翼展和相同的机身长度、宽度和高度。因此不能责怪旁观者将其中一人误认为另一人。
空中客车公司也特意以这种方式开发了这两款机型，这些保留的功能使得航空公司在其机队中运营这两种变体在操作上可行。例如，尺寸不变意味着机场可以使用相同的登机口间距和地面设备。它还简化了机组人员培训，因为飞行员可以驾驶任一型号，而无需接受完全单独的类型评级培训。
选择空中客车公司的 A321XLR 和 A321neo 规格
两者之间存在关键区别，这就是为什么 XLR 具有更强的航程和更高的最大起飞重量。该系列主要是通过在 XLR 上添加永久性 3,407.82 美制加仑（12,900-3 升）后中心油箱来实现的，这也解释了重量的增加；空客还开发了更新的燃油系统，并为该型号配备了必要的结构加固。最终，XLR 的最大航程达到 4,700 海里（8,700 公里），这是 NEO 的显着进步。
但有几家航空公司在短途航线上安排 A321XLR
因此，航空公司选择在短途航线上使用 A321XLR 的任何情况都可能看起来违反直觉。事实上，XLR 是专门为扩大 A320 系列的顶级范围而设计的。即便如此，许多航空公司在实践中确实使用该变体来实现此目的。
例如，加拿大航空部分使用 XLR 连接渥太华麦克唐纳卡地亚国际机场 (YOW) 和多伦多皮尔逊国际机场 (YYZ)，以及蒙特利尔特鲁多国际机场 (YUL) 和多伦多。每趟旅程分别持续约 39 和 53 分钟，航程在 197 海里（364 公里）和 274 海里（507 公里）之间。同时，该航空公司还使用 XLR 为多伦多至特内里费南机场 (TFS) 的近 9 小时航线提供服务。

根据航空数据平台 Avi-Go 的数据，今年 7 月，爱尔兰航空 XLR 跨越大西洋执行了 300 多次飞行超过 3,100 英里（2,694 海里或 4,989 公里）的航班，以及 200 多次飞行距离 1,250 英里（1,086 海里或 2,012 公里）或更少的航班。其中包括都柏林机场 (DUB) 至纳什维尔国际机场 (BNA)，预计运行时间为 9 小时 20 分钟，还包括都柏林至伦敦希思罗机场 (LHR) 和都柏林至何塞普·塔拉德拉斯巴塞罗那 - 埃尔普拉特机场 (BCN)，分别仅持续 48 分钟和 1 小时 50 分钟。不用说，XLR 绝不仅仅用于其范围内的任何一种情况。
A321XLR 交付仍处于早期阶段
不过，加拿大航空和爱尔兰航空并不孤单。 A321XLR 运营商的常见做法是在飞行时间和距离广泛的不同航线上运行模型。至少，目前的情况是这样的。

根据航空分析师 Cirium 去年 7 月的数据，美国航空、沙特航空和威兹航空是少数几个这样做的 XLR 运营商之一。前者使用 XLR 进行的航程涵盖 540 至 1,079 海里（1,000 至 1,999 公里）和 2,700 至 3,239 海里（5,000 至 5,999 公里）以及之间的所有航程。有趣的是，这些数据显示，XLR 于 2024 年 10 月推出的客户 Iberia 是唯一一家专门使用该型号在最高 2,700 至 3,239 海里（5,000 至 5,999 公里）和 3,240 至 3,779 海里（6,000 至 6,999 公里）范围内连接的航空公司。这个月的过程。
换句话说，最有时间将飞机纳入其机队的航空公司似乎是最频繁地充分利用 XLR 航程的航空公司。不过，考虑到空中客车公司在过去几年才开始交付该模型，这并不奇怪。据我们统计，截至 11 月份撰写本文时，已向 11 家运营商交付了 500 多份订单中的 61 款。
航空公司还在犹豫 A321XLR 航班时刻表吗？
因此，那些负责将 A321XLR 纳入更广泛计划的人员最近才从实际可用的飞机中受益。尽管提前数年下的订单需要时间进行准备，但现实世界的经验几乎无法替代 - 特别是因为 XLR 在很多方面都是之前的产品无法比拟的。
就 Iberia 而言，XLR 的功能似乎比预期的更强大。 “就舞台长度而言，[这]甚至比最初计划的要好，”首席执行官马可·安东尼奥·特鲁希略此前表示。 “事实上，我们目前正在向加勒比海、圣胡安和圣多明各开展业务，最初我们并没有想到我们的航线能够到达那里。”
另一方面，加拿大航空原计划今年在多伦多和伦敦希思罗机场之间引入 XLR。然而，这家加拿大旗舰航空公司在该机型首次亮相之前就取消了该机型，而是选择暂时坚持使用窄体飞机。所有这些都表明，提前规划是一回事，但实时满足运营要求可能完全是另一回事。

title_en: The True Cost Airbus Charges For An A330neo Compared With Boeing's 787-9 Dreamliner
title_zh: 空客 A330neo 与波音 787-9 梦想飞机的真实成本比较
summary: The cost of widebody airliners depends on the specific airline environment in which they operate, where even small marginal differences can matter.
summary_zh: 宽体客机的成本取决于其运营的具体航空公司环境，即使很小的边际差异也可能产生影响。
body_en: Aaron is an aviation enthusiast and world traveler with a deep interest in aerospace history and technology. He has traveled around the world numerous times, often incorporating visits to aviation museums and historic aircraft collections into his journeys. A native of New Zealand, he is an expert in aviation and maintains a broad interest in a variety of other subjects.

The Airbus A330-900 (A330neo) and the Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner are very close competitors. On the face of it, the 787-9 has a much larger order book (1,493 vs 511), has a noticeably higher market value, and is a cleansheet aircraft. This could be interpreted as suggesting the 787-9 has a cost advantage over the A330-900. However, the truth is more complicated, and it allows the A330-900 to remain competitive.

As Simple Flying has previously highlighted, headline list figures are an unreliable method to determine the true costs and value of aircraft and aero engines. To faithfully answer the headline of this article, list prices need to be set aside in favor of market prices and lease rates. The aviation industry runs on very thin margins. Consequently, averaging the costs of these two aircraft without considering the contingent variables of the airline in question will likely provide highly misleading numbers.

To understand why list prices are not particularly useful, it is necessary to understand what they are. An aircraft manufacturer’s list price is the published, baseline 'sticker price' for a new aircraft before negotiated discounts, rebates, or custom configuration changes. These are typically inflated prices where the manufacturer is essentially saying, " this is what we value our product at, " even though it realistically never sells them at that price and airlines and lessors would never pay it.

For an analogy, think of an airline offering the chance to win a holiday package " valued at $10,000 ." That figure may include estimates for tours, accommodation, flights, transfers, etc., all priced at the highest retail price. In practice, the airline would likely be utilizing spare capacity, receiving bulk discounts, and having special pricing arrangements, so it's only paying a fraction of the headline figure.

Likewise, holidaymakers may be able to book their own analogous trip at a fraction of the cost. List prices are similar, although they may provide a starting point in complex aircraft negotiations. As discussed below, sometimes the airplane manufacturer (Airbus, Boeing) has significant bargaining power in negotiations, while at other times the balance can swing to the customer (e.g., Emirates vis-à-vis the 777-9) .

Currently, the market values for Boeing 787-9s and A330neos are unusually high due to production bottlenecks at Airbus and Boeing. IBA writes, " This has pushed the expected delivery dates for many recent orders as far back as early 2030. With hampered production rates, it comes as no surprise that this has, in turn, allowed for Market Values and MLRs to rally over the years ." The value of widebody aircraft has grown especially fast over the last year.

In a November 2026 update, IBA reported, " Constrained supply is supporting trading values, with 2026 market values up 7% for the 787-9, 5% for the A350-900, 24% for the 777-300ER and 20% for the A330-300, alongside rising lease rates ." This shows a significant increase in market value for the older A330-300 cousin to the A330neo, but fails to include the A330neo price increase.
Cost comparison (per IBA, My Air Trade, Green Airlines )

While it's unclear how much the A330-900's market value has increased recently, its market lease rates are up by as much as 13%. The monthly market lease rate for a new Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner is around $1.05-$1.16 million, and around $900,000-$990,000 for the A330neo. At mid-age, the 787-9's rate is around $695,000-$792,000, while the A330neo is around $600,000-$756,000 per month.
Market Values Of New & Used A330-900s & 787-9s

In Q1 2026, for a newly delivered Airbus A330-900, IBA ascribed a market value of $118.5 million. Meanwhile, a new Boeing 787-9 is expected to trade in the region of $160 million . Overall, the new-delivery market value of a Boeing 787-9 is estimated to be in the $151–$160 million range by different industry analysts. The new-delivery market value range of an A330-900 (A330neo) is around $118.5–$119 million.

For comparison, the market value for larger 787-10 new-builds is around $168 million, or about $8 million more than the standard 787-9. The new value of the short 787-8 is around $116 million, or almost the same as a new A330-900. My Air Trade shows that the oldest 787-9 is estimated at around $70.6 million, while the oldest A330-900 is valued at around $73 million.

The oldest second-hand examples are estimated to be $47 million for the 787-8 and $95 million for the 787-10. No market values are given for the unpopular A330-800 variant, perhaps due to the limited deliveries and lack of market trading for the aircraft. Separately, the market values for the A380 are very low. The oldest A380s are estimated to be worth $12 million, and the most valuable are around $45 million. Put another way, a new A330-900 is worth around 3x-10x that of the world's remaining A380s.

The A330-900 and Boeing 787-9 compete on the market for a similar (but not the same) market segment . These aircraft are similar in length and have comparable typical 3-class seating capacities: 260-300 for the A330-900 and 250-290 for the 787-9. The maximum seating is around 460 and 420, respectively. In practice, the 787-9s are typically assigned more to flagship routes than the A330neo and are configured with an average of 264 seats, compared with the A330-900's denser 281-seat average.

They have almost identical maximum take-off weights (251 tonnes vs 254 tonnes) and are both very competitive in terms of cargo capacity. The Boeing 787-9 is deemed to have a modest advantage in range, although that only matters in edge cases, as most missions are well within the A330neo's maximum range. When it comes to fuel burn, it depends heavily on payload, configuration, and range. As a rule, the 787-9's fuel advantage grows with longer ranges.

One of the biggest differences is that the 787-9 is a fundamentally cleansheet composite aircraft, while the A330neo is a comprehensive update on the 1980s-designed A330. The A330neo has new engines, new wings, new avionics, and other updates, but it still has an older architecture and a mostly aluminum fuselage.

It is impossible to put a precise figure on how much the A330-900 and 787-9 cost to operate relative to each other. Too much is contingent. Even setting aside that these aircraft are better optimized for different routes and missions, many airline-specific factors matter. One important factor is the composition of the airline's overall fleet.
body_zh: 亚伦是一位航空爱好者和环球旅行家，对航空航天历史和技术有着浓厚的兴趣。他曾多次环游世界，经常在旅途中参观航空博物馆和历史飞机收藏。他是新西兰人，是航空专家，并对其他各种学科保持着广泛的兴趣。
空客 A330-900 (A330neo) 和波音 787-9 梦想飞机是非常接近的竞争对手。从表面上看，787-9 的订单量要大得多（1,493 架对 511 架），市场价值明显更高，而且是一架干净的飞机。这可以解释为表明 787-9 比 A330-900 具有成本优势。然而，事实更为复杂，这使得 A330-900 能够保持竞争力。

As Simple Flying has previously highlighted, headline list figures are an unreliable method to determine the true costs and value of aircraft and aero engines.为了忠实地回答本文的标题，需要将标价放在一边以支持市场价格和租赁率。航空业的利润非常微薄。因此，在不考虑相关航空公司的或有变量的情况下对这两架飞机的成本进行平均可能会提供极具误导性的数字。
要了解为什么标价不是特别有用，有必要了解标价是什么。飞机制造商的标价是新飞机在协商折扣、回扣或定制配置更改之前公布的基准“标价”。这些通常是虚高的价格，制造商本质上是在说，“这就是我们对我们产品的评价”，尽管它实际上从未以这个价格出售产品，航空公司和出租人也永远不会支付这个价格。
打个比方，想象一家航空公司提供赢得“价值 10,000 美元”的度假套餐的机会。该数字可能包括旅游、住宿、航班、接送等的估计，所有价格均按最高零售价计算。实际上，该航空公司可能会利用闲置产能，获得批量折扣，并进行特殊的定价安排，因此它只支付总体数字的一小部分。
同样，度假者也可以以低廉的价格预订自己的类似旅行。标价相似，尽管它们可能为复杂的飞机谈判提供一个起点。如下文所述，有时飞机制造商（空客、波音）在谈判中具有很大的议价能力，而有时，平衡可能会转向客户（例如，阿联酋航空相对于 777-9）。
目前，由于空客和波音的生产瓶颈，波音787-9和A330neo的市场价值异常高。 IBA 写道：“这使得许多近期订单的预计交货日期推迟到了 2030 年初。由于生产率受到阻碍，这反过来又使得市场价值和 MLR 多年来不断上涨，这一点也就不足为奇了。”去年，宽体飞机的价值增长尤其迅速。
IBA 在 2026 年 11 月的更新中报告称，“供应紧张正在支撑交易价值，2026 年 787-9 的市场价值将上涨 7%，A350-900 的市场价值将上涨 5%，777-300ER 的市场价值将上涨 24%，A330-300 的市场价值将上涨 20%，同时租赁率也会上涨。”这表明 A330neo 的老款 A330-300 的市场价值显着增加，但未包括 A330neo 的价格上涨。
成本比较（根据 IBA、My Air Trade、Green Airlines）

虽然目前尚不清楚A330-900的市场价值近期上涨了多少，但其市场租赁率上涨了13%之多。新型波音 787-9 梦想飞机的月市场租赁价格约为 1.05-116 万美元，A330neo 的月市场租赁价格约为 900,000-990,000 美元。到了中期，787-9 的月费约为 695,000 美元至 792,000 美元，而 A330neo 的月费约为 600,000 美元至 756,000 美元。
全新和二手 A330-900 和 787-9 的市场价值
2026 年第一季度，新交付的空客 A330-900 的市场价值为 1.185 亿美元。与此同时，一架新的波音 787-9 预计售价约为 1.6 亿美元。总体而言，不同行业分析师估计波音 787-9 的新交付市场价值在 151 至 1.6 亿美元之间。新交付的 A330-900 (A330neo) 的市场价值范围约为 118.5 至 1.19 亿美元。
相比之下，较大型新建 787-10 的市场价值约为 1.68 亿美元，比标准 787-9 多出约 800 万美元。短款 787-8 的新价值约为 1.16 亿美元，几乎与新的 A330-900 相同。我的 Air Trade 显示，最老的 787-9 的估价约为 7060 万美元，而最老的 A330-900 的估价约为 7300 万美元。
最古老的二手飞机 787-8 估计价值 4700 万美元，787-10 价值 9500 万美元。不受欢迎的 A330-800 型号没有给出市场价值，可能是由于该飞机的交付量有限且缺乏市场交易。另外，A380 的市场价值非常低。最老的 A380 估计价值 1200 万美元，最有价值的约为 4500 万美元。换句话说，新型 A330-900 的价值约为世界上剩余 A380 的 3 至 10 倍。

A330-900 和波音 787-9 在市场上竞争相似（但不相同）的细分市场。这些飞机的长度相似，并且具有与典型 3 舱座位数相当的容量：A330-900 为 260-300 人，787-9 为 250-290 人。最大座位数分别约为 460 和 420。实际上，787-9 通常比 A330neo 分配更多的旗舰航线，平均配置 264 个座位，而 A330-900 的平均座位数更密集，为 281 个座位。
它们的最大起飞重量几乎相同（251 吨与 254 吨），并且在载货能力方面都非常有竞争力。波音 787-9 被认为在航程方面具有一定的优势，尽管这只在边缘情况下才重要，因为大多数任务都在 A330neo 的最大航程范围内。当谈到燃油消耗时，它在很大程度上取决于有效载荷、配置和航程。一般来说，787-9 的燃油优势随着航程的增加而增加。
最大的区别之一是 787-9 基本上是一款全新的复合材料飞机，而 A330neo 是 1980 年代设计的 A330 的全面更新。 A330neo 拥有新的发动机、新的机翼、新的航空电子设备和其他更新，但它仍然具有较旧的架构和大部分铝制机身。
不可能准确计算出 A330-900 和 787-9 相对运行成本是多少。太多是偶然的。即使不考虑这些飞机针对不同航线和任务进行了更好的优化，许多航空公司特定的因素也很重要。一个重要因素是航空公司整个机队的构成。

title_en: Why Delta Air Lines Quietly Added ETOPS Certification To Its Boeing 737-900ERs Even Though They Don't Fly Transatlantic & Pacific Legs
title_zh: 为什么达美航空悄悄为其波音 737-900ER 增加了 ETOPS 认证，尽管它们不飞越大西洋和太平洋航线
summary: How the carrier manages its ETOPS narrowbody fleet.
summary_zh: 该航空公司如何管理其 ETOPS 窄体机机队。
body_en: Daniel comes to Simple Flying with a business focused approach to the aviation world. Daniel enjoys analyzing strategy and how companies move against each other to gain a step ahead in the skies. Besides strategy, Daniel also has a passion for aircraft design and the history of aviation.

In 2011, Delta Air Lines announced an order for 100 Boeing 737-900ERs , the largest variant of the 737 family. It later ordered another 20 units in 2015 and another 10 in 2017, bringing its total to 130, and the airline acquired another 33 second-hand aircraft after COVID. They first started arriving in 2013, and the large, efficient 737-900ER has become a workhorse for Delta's domestic network. The type, however, isn't known for exceptional range and flies only within North America. Yet, these aircraft are certified for ETOPS-180 operations.

ETOPS stands for Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards (or alternatively, Engines Turn Or Passengers Swim), and ETOPS certification demonstrates that a twin-engine aircraft may safely fly more than 60 minutes from a diversion airfield. The number denotes how far the aircraft may fly from an airfield in minutes. Although the 737-900ER does not operate any transoceanic flights, Delta has chosen to maintain ETOPS certification on some of its 737-900ERs, but not all of them.

Modern twinjets are certified by regulators with an ETOPS type design approval, but this doesn't mean that a specific aircraft is ETOPS-certified . Planes need to be individually approved for ETOPS operations, as the regulator needs to verify that the aircraft features special equipment mandatory for overwater operations and that the airline has procedures in place that comply with ETOPS practices. An airline could even choose to have just one aircraft certified for ETOPS, or it could certify its entire fleet if desired.

The ETOPS certification process is expensive, and the extra equipment adds weight to the aircraft. Therefore, airlines generally only certify aircraft with ETOPS if the aircraft will regularly operate overwater flights to make the investment worth it. As an example, all of Delta's widebodies are ETOPS certified, but many of its short-haul aircraft are not. Notably, however, the 737-900ER lacks the range to operate transoceanic routes and is primarily used for domestic services.

But although the 737-900ER is not generally known for having long range, the aircraft is still capable of operating longer services. This includes transcontinental flights or services to the Caribbean.

While ETOPS is not generally necessary for Caribbean flights, it can permit more efficient routings in some cases, and the 737-900ER is still commonly deployed on the carrier's routes to this region. In addition, while the role of the 737-900ER has been changing as Delta receives a higher number of new narrowbody aircraft, the carrier formerly had a majority of its 737-900ERs ETOPS certified.

Today, Delta only maintains a small subfleet of roughly 20 737-900ERs with ETOPS certification, while the remaining are not certified for extended overwater operations. However, many of these planes formerly featured equipment for ETOPS operations and were maintained to ETOPS-180 standards. Delta later removed the extra equipment from many of its 737s and no longer holds them to ETOPS standards.

The 737-900ER was Delta's newest and most economical large narrowbody in the mid-2010s. With such a large order, the Atlanta-based carrier intended to deploy the 737-900ER throughout its network on some of its longest routes within North America. Some of these are Caribbean services that would require ETOPS certification for more efficient routings; hence, most of the 737-900ERs got ETOPS certification. In addition, Delta also originally intended to use the 737-900ER for some of its services to Hawaii from the West Coast, which necessitates ETOPS-180.

ETOPS equipment and maintaining ETOPS certification for an aircraft is expensive, so Delta has removed it from most 737s as the airline uses the 737 on fewer overwater routes today. Part of this is because the carrier now has a large Airbus A321neo fleet, which has been deployed on longer Caribbean routes due to its excellent fuel efficiency. The other reason is that the previously planned Hawaii services didn't work out, and Delta pulled the 737s from these operations.

Until the arrival of the 737-900ER, Delta primarily relied on the far less efficient 757 for its routes from the West Coast to Hawaii. In 2016, the airline began scheduling the 737-900ER on flights between Seattle and Honolulu, while the 737 began flying to Kona shortly afterwards. However, the airline would end up pulling the 737-900ER off of these routes, instead replacing it with the 757 again, as these routes pushed the 737-900ER too far past its payload-range limitations.

The 737-900ER can and has operated longer routes than these Hawaii services, even for Delta itself. However, operating an ETOPS flight requires extra fuel reserves; in the case of the Hawaii routes, the aircraft needs to carry enough fuel to essentially turn around midway, as there are no diversion airports between the West Coast and Hawaii. The fuel reserves add significant weight, cutting into payload, and the 737-900ERs were frequently payload-restricted when flying to Hawaii, hurting revenue.

United Airlines also faced this same issue when operating the 737-900ER to Hawaii, but the Chicago-based carrier had a smaller 757 fleet than Delta, and most of its examples were configured with lie-flat business class seats. Delta, with its large subfleets of domestic-configured 757s, was able to switch the routes back to the 757s, which cost more to operate but also earned more revenue. Today, Delta mainly relies on the A321neo for its Hawaii routes, while United relies on the 737 MAX, neither of which faces these issues.

Delta Air Lines uses the A321neo, 737-900ER, and 757 for routes to the Caribbean and Hawaii. Because its network of overwater routes within North America is operated by several types, the airline maintains subfleets of planes with ETOPS certification and planes without. Only about half of the A321neos are certified for ETOPS operations, as well as select 737s and 757s. As a whole, just over 100 of Delta's 828 narrowbodies are certified for ETOPS, because this is all that the airline needs.

United Airlines , however, certifies all of its 640 737s and 61 757s for ETOPS operations . The 737s are the airline's primary aircraft for Caribbean and Hawaii routes, while the 757-200 is heavily used to Europe. The 757-300s are also still used on several of United's flights to Hawaii. Still, the carrier has significantly more ETOPS-certified aircraft than it likely needs; it even maintains ETOPS certification on its 12 737-900s, which mainly operate short domestic trips out of Houston. This is a costlier approach, but what it allows is operational flexibility.
body_zh: Daniel 带着以商业为中心的方式进入航空界，加入了 Simple Flying。丹尼尔喜欢分析战略以及公司如何相互竞争以取得领先一步。除了战略之外，丹尼尔还对飞机设计和航空历史充满热情。

2011 年，达美航空宣布订购 100 架波音 737-900ER，这是 737 系列中最大的型号。随后，该航空公司于 2015 年又订购了 20 架，并于 2017 年又订购了 10 架，使总数达到 130 架，并在新冠疫情之后又购买了 33 架二手飞机。它们于 2013 年首次抵达，大型高效的 737-900ER 已成为达美航空国内网络的主力飞机。然而，这种类型并不以超凡的航程而闻名，并且仅在北美范围内飞行。然而，这些飞机已获得 ETOPS-180 运行认证。
ETOPS 代表增程双引擎运行性能标准（或者，发动机转动或乘客游泳），ETOPS 认证表明双引擎飞机可以从改航机场安全飞行 60 分钟以上。该数字表示飞机在几分钟内可以从机场飞多远。尽管 737-900ER 不运营任何跨洋航班，但达美航空已选择在部分（但不是全部）737-900ER 上保留 ETOPS 认证。
现代双发飞机已获得监管机构的 ETOPS 型式设计批准认证，但这并不意味着特定飞机已获得 ETOPS 认证。飞机需要单独获得 ETOPS 运营批准，因为监管机构需要验证飞机是否配备水上运营所需的特殊设备，以及航空公司是否制定了符合 ETOPS 实践的程序。航空公司甚至可以选择只让一架飞机获得 ETOPS 认证，或者如果需要，也可以对其整个机队进行认证。
ETOPS 认证过程成本高昂，而且额外的设备会增加飞机的重量。因此，航空公司通常只会在飞机定期执行水上飞行以使投资物有所值的情况下才对具有ETOPS的飞机进行认证。例如，达美航空的所有宽体飞机都经过 ETOPS 认证，但许多短途飞机却没有。但值得注意的是，737-900ER 缺乏运营跨洋航线的航程，主要用于国内航班。
尽管 737-900ER 并不以航程长而闻名，但该飞机仍然能够执行更长时间的服务。这包括飞往加勒比海的跨大陆航班或服务。
虽然加勒比航班通常不需要 ETOPS，但在某些情况下它可以实现更高效的航线，并且 737-900ER 仍然普遍部署在该航空公司飞往该地区的航线上。此外，虽然随着达美航空接收更多数量的新型窄体飞机，737-900ER 的角色一直在发生变化，但该航空公司之前大部分 737-900ER 都经过了 ETOPS 认证。
如今，达美航空仅拥有约 20 架 737-900ER 的小型子机队，拥有 ETOPS 认证，而其余机队则未获得长期水上运营认证。然而，其中许多飞机以前配备了用于 ETOPS 操作的设备，并按照 ETOPS-180 标准进行维护。达美航空后来从其许多 737 飞机上拆除了额外的设备，并不再要求它们符合 ETOPS 标准。

737-900ER 是达美航空 2010 年代中期最新、最经济的大型窄体飞机。有了如此大的订单，这家总部位于亚特兰大的航空公司打算在其北美境内一些最长航线的整个网络中部署 737-900ER。其中一些是加勒比地区的服务，需要 ETOPS 认证才能实现更高效的航线；因此，大多数 737-900ER 获得了 ETOPS 认证。此外，达美航空原本还打算使用737-900ER来执行其从西海岸飞往夏威夷的部分航班，因此需要ETOPS-180。
ETOPS 设备和维持飞机的 ETOPS 认证费用昂贵，因此达美航空已将其从大多数 737 飞机上删除，因为该航空公司目前在水上航线上使用 737 的数量较少。部分原因是该航空公司现在拥​​有一支庞大的空客A321neo机队，由于其出色的燃油效率，该机队已部署在较长的加勒比航线上。另一个原因是之前计划的夏威夷航班未能成功，达美航空将 737 飞机从这些运营中撤下。
在 737-900ER 到来之前，达美航空主要依靠效率低得多的 757 来运营从西海岸到夏威夷的航线。 2016 年，该航空公司开始安排 737-900ER 执飞西雅图和檀香山之间的航班，而 737 不久后又开始飞往科纳。然而，该航空公司最终将 737-900ER 从这些航线上撤下，而是再次用 757 取而代之，因为这些航线使 737-900ER 远远超出了其有效载荷范围限制。
737-900ER 能够并且已经运营了比这些夏威夷航班更长的航线，甚至达美航空本身也是如此。然而，运行 ETOPS 航班需要额外的燃油储备；就夏威夷航线而言，飞机需要携带足够的燃油才能中途掉头，因为西海岸和夏威夷之间没有改航机场。燃油储备显着增加了重量，减少了有效载荷，而且 737-900ER 在飞往夏威夷时经常受到有效载荷限制，从而损害了收入。

美国联合航空在运营飞往夏威夷的 737-900ER 飞机时也面临同样的问题，但这家总部位于芝加哥的航空公司的 757 机队规模比达美航空要小，而且大多数机型都配置了平躺式商务舱座椅。达美航空拥有大量国内配置的 757 飞机，能够将航线改回 757 飞机，虽然运营成本更高，但也获得了更多收入。如今，达美航空在夏威夷航线上主要依靠 A321neo，而美联航则依靠 737 MAX，两者都没有面临这些问题。

达美航空使用 A321neo、737-900ER 和 757 执飞飞往加勒比海和夏威夷的航线。由于其北美境内的水上航线网络由多种类型运营，因此该航空公司拥有拥有 ETOPS 认证和未获得 ETOPS 认证的飞机的子机队。只有大约一半的 A321neo 以及部分 737 和 757 获得了 ETOPS 运行认证。总体而言，达美航空 828 架窄体机中只有 100 多架获得了 ETOPS 认证，因为这就是该航空公司所需要的全部。

然而，联合航空对其所有 640 737 和 61 757 进行了 ETOPS 运营认证。 737 是该航空公司加勒比和夏威夷航线的主要飞机，而 757-200 则大量用于欧洲航线。美联航飞往夏威夷的几趟航班仍在使用 757-300。尽管如此，该航空公司拥有的 ETOPS 认证飞机数量仍远远超出了其可能的需求；该公司甚至在其 12 737-900 飞机上保持了 ETOPS 认证，这些飞机主要运营休斯顿以外的短途国内航班。这是一种成本较高的方法，但它允许操作灵活性。

title_en: Delta Air Lines Flight Halts Taxi In Boston After Cat Escapes Kennel, Runs Loose In Cabin
title_zh: 猫逃离狗窝并在机舱内逃逸后，达美航空航班在波士顿停止出租车
summary: "Have a good day, meow": an unusual situation gives controllers a laugh.
summary_zh: “祝你有美好的一天，喵”：不寻常的情况让管制员大笑。
body_en: Jack comes to Simple Flying with a lifelong interest in all things aviation. He holds a degree in Aerospace Engineering from Georgia Tech, and is a certified private and remote pilot. Beyond these experiences, Jack previously worked for a corporate flight department where he gained first-hand experience in the world of business aviation. Currently, Jack works in the professional services industry and continues to build his flight hours outside of work.

A Delta Air Lines flight bound for Tampa stopped on a taxiway at Boston Logan International Airport (BOS) on Friday morning after a cat escaped its kennel and roamed the cabin. Delta flight 2706 was preparing to depart at about 7:00 AM when the animal got loose, and the crew held the aircraft until the cat was secured, delaying departure by roughly 15 minutes. The flight still reached Tampa on time, according to a Delta spokesperson.

Air traffic control audio captured the exchange, in which the captain told controllers the aircraft had a situation in the cabin and needed to hold. Once the cat was back in its kennel, the captain thanked ground control for accommodating the stop, and a controller, who called the episode “ a new one ,” closed with a feline pun, wishing the crew a good day.

The controller directed the aircraft straight ahead to hold short of taxiway Foxtrot and then told the crew to monitor the tower frequency, according to the recorded exchange . The controller offered assistance, but the captain declined, indicating that the crew regarded the problem as manageable without outside help. The captain initially asked only to hold somewhere for a minute, which suggests the crew expected a brief resolution.

Delta told Boston local news stations WCVB and WMTW that the plane was moving toward the runway when the cat left its carrier and wandered the cabin until it was herded back. Delta did not immediately explain how the animal was caught, and the sources reviewed do not say whether the kennel was damaged or how long the cat remained loose.

After the cat was secured, the pilot asked to rejoin the departure sequence, and the aircraft resumed taxiing and departed normally. Resolving the problem before takeoff matters operationally, because an unrestrained animal moving through a cabin during climb could interfere with cabin crew duties and passenger seating, an assessment based on standard cabin procedures rather than anything Delta stated.

Delta’s pet policy requires customers to keep an animal calm and secured inside its kennel at all times in the airport, including during check-in, boarding, and deplaning, in a Sky Club , and aboard the aircraft. The kennel must fit fully under the seat directly in front of the customer, and its maximum dimensions depend on the aircraft type. Delta also says under-seat space varies by aircraft, so a kennel that fits one type may not fit another. The animal must be small enough to move around in the kennel without touching or protruding from its sides, and the owner may bring one personal item or one carry-on in addition to the kennel. Delta also limits the number of pets on each flight and assigns space on a first-come basis.

According to Delta’s trade guidance, passengers with carry-on pets cannot sit in bulkhead seats, exit rows, seats designated as no stowage, or flat-bed seats, and the kennel door must remain secured throughout boarding, lounge visits, and the flight. Pets must be at least eight weeks old for domestic travel, and each kennel may hold one pet, with narrow exceptions such as young litters. Delta warns that failing to follow the rules may cost a traveler the ability to bring a pet on future flights, although the sources reviewed do not say whether the owner in this case faces any consequence.

Mediaite framed the episode as welcome levity after the FAA’s November 13 nationwide ground stop, which had prompted passengers to question the safety of air travel. The audio spread after an aviation news account on social media shared what appeared to be a conversation between the aircraft and controllers. Delta confirmed the sequence of events through spokespeople to several outlets, but none of the reports reviewed include a statement from passengers aboard the flight.

Delta says relief areas are available at most airports, and after the security checkpoint, a pet must stay in its kennel unless it is in one of those designated areas. For owners of anxious animals, that guidance makes the pre-boarding period the main opportunity to let a pet out safely, because the cabin offers none.
body_zh: Jack 带着对航空一切事物的终生兴趣加入了 Simple Flying。他拥有佐治亚理工学院的航空航天工程学位，并且是一名经过认证的私人和远程飞行员。除了这些经验之外，杰克还曾在公司飞行部门工作过，在那里他获得了公务航空领域的第一手经验。目前，杰克在专业服务行业工作，并在工作之外继续增加飞行时间。
周五早上，达美航空一架飞往坦帕的航班在波士顿洛根国际机场 (BOS) 的滑行道上停了下来，原因是一只猫逃离了狗窝并在机舱里闲逛。早上 7:00 左右，达美航空 2706 航班正准备起飞，这只猫却逃脱了，机组人员控制住了飞机，直到猫被固定住，导致起飞时间延迟了大约 15 分钟。达美航空发言人表示，该航班仍然准时抵达坦帕。
空中交通管制音频捕捉到了这次交流，机长告诉管制员，飞机机舱内出现情况，需要等待。当猫回到狗窝后，机长感谢地面控制人员安排了这次停留，一名控制人员称这一事件为“新事件”，并用猫科动物的双关语结束了这一事件，祝愿机组人员有美好的一天。
根据交流记录，管制员指示飞机直线前进，在滑行道 Foxtrot 附近停留，然后告诉机组人员监控塔台频率。管制员提供了帮助，但机长拒绝了，这表明机组人员认为无需外部帮助即可解决问题。船长最初只要求在某处停留一分钟，这表明船员们希望得到一个简短的解决方案。
达美航空告诉波士顿当地新闻台 WCVB 和 WMTW，飞机正在驶向跑道时，这只猫离开了机舱，在机舱里徘徊，直到被赶回来。达美航空没有立即解释这只动物是如何被抓到的，所审查的消息来源也没有说明狗舍是否遭到损坏，也没有说明这只猫被释放了多长时间。
猫被固定后，飞行员要求重新加入起飞序列，飞机恢复滑行并正常起飞。在起飞前解决问题对于操作来说很重要，因为在爬升过程中不受约束的动物在机舱内移动可能会干扰机组人员的职责和乘客座位，这是基于标准机舱程序而不是达美航空所说的任何评估。

达美航空的宠物政策要求乘客在机场任何时候都必须将动物保持在宠物笼内并确保其安全，包括办理登机手续、登机和下机期间、在天空俱乐部以及飞机上。狗窝必须完全安装在乘客正前方的座椅下方，其最大尺寸取决于飞机类型。达美航空还表示，座位下的空间因飞机而异，因此适合一种类型的狗窝可能不适合另一种类型。动物必须足够小，可以在狗舍内移动，而不会接触或从其侧面突出，并且除了狗舍外，主人还可以携带一件个人物品或一件随身携带的物品。达美航空还限制每次航班携带的宠物数量，并按照先到先得的原则分配空间。
根据达美航空的贸易指南，携带宠物登机的乘客不能坐在舱壁座位、出口排座位、指定为不可装载的座位或平板座位上，并且在整个登机、休息室和飞行过程中，宠物箱门必须保持安全。国内旅行的宠物必须至少八周大，每个狗舍可以容纳一只宠物，但有极少数例外，例如幼崽。达美航空警告称，不遵守规定可能会导致旅客无法在未来的航班上携带宠物，不过所审查的消息来源并未透露本案中的宠物主人是否会面临任何后果。
Mediaite 将这一事件描述为美国联邦航空局 11 月 13 日在全国范围内进行地面停车后值得欢迎的玩笑，这引发了乘客对航空旅行安全性的质疑。社交媒体上的一个航空新闻账户分享了飞机和管制员之间的一段对话后，这段音频就传开了。达美航空通过发言人向多家媒体证实了事件的顺序，但所审查的报告均未包含航班上乘客的声明。
达美航空表示，大多数机场都设有救援区，在通过安全检查点后，宠物必须留在宠物笼中，除非它位于这些指定区域之一。对于焦虑动物的主人来说，这种指导使登机前的时间成为让宠物安全离开的主要机会，因为机舱不提供这种指导。

title_en: Boeing Weighs More Layoffs As 737 MAX Output Boost Slows
title_zh: 由于 737 MAX 产量增长放缓，波音考虑进一步裁员
summary: The company is struggling to lift output to its target monthly number.
summary_zh: 该公司正在努力将产量提高到月度目标。
body_en: Jack comes to Simple Flying with a lifelong interest in all things aviation. He holds a degree in Aerospace Engineering from Georgia Tech, and is a certified private and remote pilot. Beyond these experiences, Jack previously worked for a corporate flight department where he gained first-hand experience in the world of business aviation. Currently, Jack works in the professional services industry and continues to build his flight hours outside of work.

Boeing declined on Thursday to tell one of its largest unions whether further layoffs will follow a round planned for next month, even as the company struggles to lift 737 MAX output from 42 jets a month to 47, a rate it had expected to reach this past summer. The company announced this month that it would cut 5% of the roughly 50,000 employees in its commercial airplanes division, and now expects to reach 47 jets a month in early 2027, according to Reuters .

Bryan Corliss, a spokesperson for the Society of Professional Engineering Employees in Aerospace (SPEEA), said the union asked whether December 9 was the only date for layoff notices and was told Boeing did not know. Managers told union officials that employment at every commercial airplane site is under review, that the cuts will be targeted at work statements that are ending or can be ended rather than applied across the board, and that no voluntary layoffs or buyouts will be offered.

The 737 MAX is Boeing’s best-selling jet, and the company had planned to reach the 47-a-month rate by summer 2026. The bottleneck behind the delay is the wing line , where Chief Executive Kelly Ortberg told analysts in late October that Boeing was not yet stably producing wings at the volume needed for 47 jets a month, while acknowledging that some process improvements meant to speed flow had not delivered the expected savings. Boeing will miss its 2026 production and delivery targets, and Chief Financial Officer Jay Malave said the company will fall short of its goal of delivering 500 737s this year, though the company has not said by how much.

A shortage of wings also limits the usefulness of added assembly staff, since downstream workers can't build jets without them, which helps explain why strong demand and layoffs can coexist. The longer-term schedule has moved accordingly, since Boeing is targeting 52 jets a month in the second half of 2027 and Ortberg said the company must first demonstrate sustained performance at 47, with no significant increase in output expected before then.

Stephanie Pope, chief executive of Boeing Commercial Airplanes, told employees in a November 9 memo that the division would reduce headcount by roughly 5% through attrition and involuntary layoffs, with notifications starting in December. She said adjusting production schedules and lowering output leaves the unit overstaffed, and that Boeing needed to reset its ramp pace to give factories and suppliers more time to stabilize. Pope also noted that Boeing has made significant investments in talent, training, and infrastructure over the past two years, framing the reduction as a recalibration rather than a retreat.

Boeing has not published a headcount target, and it has declined to name affected locations, divisions, or programs. Applying 5% to the 50,494 people the division employed in December 2025 implies about 2,500 positions, a figure reported by observers rather than confirmed by the company. The reset also affects suppliers, whose own schedules were built around a faster ramp, although the sources reviewed do not quantify any changes to supplier orders.

The timing is sensitive for the labor relationship, because SPEEA, which represents engineers and technical employees at Boeing, ratified a new four-year contract in early October, roughly five weeks before the layoff announcement. The agreement includes a guaranteed 10% raise upon ratification, annual increases of 4%, and a possible additional 2% tied to performance. Boeing managers told the union that the layoffs are not retaliation for that agreement.

The backdrop is unusual for a manufacturer with strong demand, since a record backlog of $745 billion was reported alongside the cuts. That pairing suggests the constraint is throughput, not orders, and it frames what to watch next: whether the December 9 notices are the last, whether wing output holds at 47 in early 2027, and whether the step to 52 arrives on schedule in the second half of that year. Boeing’s fourth-quarter results should offer the next formal update on that timeline.
body_zh: Jack 带着对航空一切事物的终生兴趣加入了 Simple Flying。他拥有佐治亚理工学院的航空航天工程学位，并且是一名经过认证的私人和远程飞行员。除了这些经验之外，杰克还曾在公司飞行部门工作过，在那里他获得了公务航空领域的第一手经验。目前，杰克在专业服务行业工作，并在工作之外继续增加飞行时间。
波音公司周四拒绝透露其最大的工会之一是否会在下个月计划的一轮裁员之后进一步裁员，尽管该公司正在努力将 737 MAX 的产量从每月 42 架飞机提高到 47 架，这是去年夏天预计会达到的水平。据路透社报道，该公司本月宣布，将在其商用飞机部门约 5 万名员工中裁员 5%，目前预计到 2027 年初，每月飞机数量将达到 47 架。
航空航天专业工程雇员协会 (SPEEA) 发言人布莱恩·科利斯 (Bryan Corliss) 表示，工会询问 12 月 9 日是否是发出裁员通知的唯一日期，并被告知波音公司并不知道。经理们告诉工会官员，每个商用飞机基地的就业情况都在接受审查，裁员将针对即将结束或可能结束的工作报表，而不是全面实施，并且不会提供自愿裁员或买断。

737 MAX 是波音最畅销的喷气式飞机，该公司原计划到 2026 年夏季达到每月 47 架的产量。延误背后的瓶颈是机翼生产线，首席执行官凯利·奥特伯格 (Kelly Ortberg) 10 月底告诉分析师，波音尚未稳定地生产每月 47 架喷气式飞机所需的机翼数量，同时承认一些旨在加快流程的流程改进并未带来预期的节省。波音公司将无法实现 2026 年的生产和交付目标，首席财务官杰伊·马拉维 (Jay Malave) 表示，该公司将无法实现今年交付 500 架 737 飞机的目标，但该公司并未透露具体数字。
机翼短缺也限制了增加装配人员的用处，因为下游工人没有他们就无法制造喷气式飞机，这有助于解释为什么强劲的需求和裁员可以并存。长期计划也相应调整，因为波音公司的目标是在 2027 年下半年每月生产 52 架飞机，奥特伯格表示，该公司必须首先展示 47 架飞机的持续绩效，在此之前预计产量不会大幅增加。

波音商用飞机公司首席执行官斯蒂芬妮·波普 (Stephanie Pope) 在 11 月 9 日的一份备忘录中告诉员工，该部门将通过自然减员和非自愿裁员将员工人数减少约 5%，并从 12 月开始发出通知。她表示，调整生产计划和降低产量导致该部门人员过剩，波音需要重新调整产能进度，以便给工厂和供应商更多时间稳定下来。波普还指出，过去两年，波音公司在人才、培训和基础设施方面进行了大量投资，将裁员视为一种重新调整，而不是撤退。
波音公司尚未公布员工人数目标，也拒绝透露受影响地点、部门或项目的名称。如果对该部门 2025 年 12 月雇用的 50,494 名员工实行 5% 的税率，则意味着大约有 2,500 个职位，这一数字是观察人士报告的，但未经公司证实。重置也会影响供应商，他们自己的时间表是围绕更快的进度制定的，尽管审查的消息来源没有量化供应商订单的任何变化。
这个时机对于劳资关系来说很敏感，因为代表波音工程师和技术员工的 SPEEA 于 10 月初批准了一份新的四年期合同，大约在宣布裁员的五周前。该协议包括批准后保证 10% 的加薪、每年 4% 的加薪以及可能与绩效挂钩的额外 2% 的加薪。波音公司经理告诉工会，裁员并不是对该协议的报复。
对于需求强劲的制造商来说，这种背景是不寻常的，因为在削减成本的同时，还有创纪录的 7,450 亿美元积压订单。这种配对表明限制因素是吞吐量，而不是订单，并且它确定了接下来要关注的内容：12 月 9 日的通知是否是最后一次，2027 年初机翼产量是否保持在 47，以及该年下半年是否按计划达到 52。波音公司第四季度业绩应该会提供该时间表的下一次正式更新。

title_en: Why Airliners Cruise Around 35,000 Feet Instead Of Flying Lower Or Higher
title_zh: 为什么客机在 35,000 英尺左右巡航而不是飞得更低或更高
summary: Why do commercial airplanes cruise at 35,000 feet? Several aerodynamic, economic and operational factors determine how high airliners can fly.
summary_zh: 为什么商用飞机要在 35,000 英尺的高度巡航？多个空气动力学、经济和运营因素决定了客机的飞行高度。
body_en: Passionate about promoting aviation, the beauty of flight and the science behind it, Antonio is an avid reader of aviation magazines and books, and he loves visiting airshows all over the world, taking photos and writing about airplanes and helicopters as well. He is currently based in Palermo, Sicily.

If you glance at the flight map on the seatback screen, the number indicating the aircraft altitude is almost always the same: 35,000 feet (10,668 meters). No law demands it, and no airline manual treats it as sacred. But jet airliners flying from Seattle to Singapore keep settling into the same narrowband of sky, as if the atmosphere came with a built-in parking spot.

The thin air that makes high-altitude flying cheaper also takes lift away from the wings and thrust away from the engines, while the safety margin narrows with every thousand feet. The result is a constant compromise between aerodynamics, engine performance, aircraft weight, winds, and air traffic control. And the altitude that makes the most sense at the beginning of a long flight may be completely different several hours later.
Thin Air Makes High-Altitude Cruise More Fuel Efficient

That compromise starts with something passengers rarely notice from the cabin: there is dramatically less atmosphere at 35,000 feet than there is at sea level. According to AirportFYI , the International Standard Atmosphere puts air at about 31% of its sea-level density at 35,000 feet, or roughly 0.024 pounds per cubic foot (0.38 kg per cubic meter). Just imagine wading through a swimming pool versus walking through an ankle-deep puddle. Less air means less drag, and drag is one of the biggest fuel penalties an aircraft has to overcome. If you prefer to see the idea rather than read it, this YouTube explainer tackles the same question visually.

That reduction in density is one reason modern airliners spend so much of their cruise above most weather systems. The cabin , of course, cannot simply follow the outside atmosphere. At 35,000 feet, the air outside is far too thin to breathe normally, which is why pressurized cabins are maintained at an equivalent altitude of roughly 6,000 to 8,000 feet (1,800 to 2,400 meters). Temperature helps the equation as well. The standard atmosphere at 35,000 feet is around minus 66°F (minus 54°C), and the speed of sound falls to about 660 mph (1,062 km/h), compared with 761 mph (1,225 km/h) at sea level. AirportFYI notes that modern swept-wing jets typically cruise between Mach 0.78 and 0.85 there, roughly 515 to 560 mph (830 to 900 km/h). As reported by Military & Aerospace Electronics , thinner air reduces drag and lets an aircraft cover more distance for the fuel it burns.

That is the attraction of altitude. But reducing the air around an aircraft also reduces the air available to its wings and engines. Eventually, climbing higher stops being an efficiency trick and becomes a performance problem.
Higher Altitudes Reduce Drag But Also Reduce Performance

The same thin air that makes cruise economical creates the next limitation. A wing still has to produce enough lift to support the aircraft, and lift depends partly on air density and the square of airspeed. At roughly 31% of sea-level density, an airliner has to fly substantially faster through the air, or operate at a higher angle of attack, to generate the lift required to carry the same weight. Military & Aerospace Electronics explains that an aircraft can compensate through speed and angle of attack, but it cannot keep climbing indefinitely and expect performance to remain unchanged.

Engines face their own problem. As Your Mileage May Vary points out, there are fewer oxygen molecules available for combustion at high altitude, reducing engine thrust. The climb itself also costs fuel, so gaining altitude is only worthwhile when the efficiency gained during cruise outweighs the energy spent getting there. NASA describes cruise efficiency as a function of the aircraft, its engines, and its operating conditions rather than a single ideal altitude.

The table also explains why flying lower is not the answer. At 10,000 feet (3,048 meters), a jet encounters more than twice the air density it does at 35,000 feet, meaning considerably more aerodynamic resistance. It is also closer to weather and other traffic. Yet the best altitude is not fixed, because the aircraft itself changes throughout the flight.
Aircraft Weight Moves The Optimum Cruise Altitude Upward

A long-haul aircraft leaves the gate carrying tons of fuel and gradually gets lighter as that fuel is burned. That changes the altitude at which it can operate most efficiently. Military & Aerospace Electronics explains that an aircraft's weight can make a higher altitude less efficient early in a flight or leave too little performance margin to climb there. NASA likewise describes optimum cruise altitude as closely tied to aircraft weight.

AirportFYI offers an illustrative example: a heavily loaded Boeing 777-300ER flying from Dubai to London might begin with an optimum altitude around FL310, or 31,000 feet (9,449 meters), before moving toward FL390, or 39,000 feet (11,887 meters), several hours later. The aircraft does not normally climb continuously. Instead, crews can make staged increases known as step climbs. AirportFYI says these steps are usually 2,000 or 4,000 feet (610 or 1,219 meters), and cites industry studies estimating that optimized step climbs on 12- to 16-hour flights can save 1% to 3% of total fuel compared with remaining at one fixed altitude.

The gradual climb reflects the aircraft's changing weight: as fuel is burned, the jet becomes lighter and can climb more efficiently. But even a progressively lighter jet eventually reaches a point where going higher brings a new problem: the two boundaries of safe high-altitude flight begin moving toward one another.
Coffin Corner Limits How High Airliners Can Efficiently Cruise

The higher an aircraft climbs, the less room it has between two very different aerodynamic problems. The first is flying too slowly and approaching a stall. The second is flying too quickly and encountering compressibility effects as the airflow over the wing approaches critical Mach. Because the speed of sound falls as temperature drops while the true airspeed required to generate lift rises in thinner air, the two boundaries eventually begin to converge.
body_zh: 安东尼奥热衷于推广航空、飞行之美及其背后的科学，是航空杂志和书籍的狂热读者，他喜欢参观世界各地的航展，也喜欢拍摄有关飞机和直升机的照片和撰写有关飞机和直升机的文章。他目前居住在西西里岛巴勒莫。
如果你看一眼座椅靠背屏幕上的飞行地图，指示飞机高度的数字几乎总是相同的：35,000 英尺（10,668 米）。没有法律要求这样做，也没有航空公司手册将其视为神圣的。但从西雅图飞往新加坡的喷气式客机不断降落在同一个狭窄的天空中，就好像大气中带有一个内置的停车位一样。
稀薄的空气使高空飞行变得更便宜，同时也带走了机翼的升力和发动机的推力，而安全裕度每增加一千英尺就会缩小。其结果是空气动力学、发动机性能、飞机重量、风和空中交通管制之间的不断妥协。在长途飞行开始时最有意义的高度可能在几个小时后就完全不同了。
稀薄的空气使高空巡航更省油

这种妥协始于乘客在机舱内很少注意到的一些事情：35,000 英尺高度的大气层比海平面的大气层少得多。根据 AirportFYI 的数据，国际标准大气在 35,000 英尺处的空气密度约为海平面密度的 31%，即每立方英尺约 0.024 磅（每立方米 0.38 千克）。想象一下涉水穿过游泳池与步行穿过齐踝深的水坑。更少的空气意味着更少的阻力，而阻力是飞机必须克服的最大燃油损失之一。如果您更喜欢看到这个想法而不是阅读它，这个 YouTube 解释器可以直观地解决相同的问题。

密度的降低是现代客机在大多数天气系统上花费大量巡航时间的原因之一。当然，小屋不能简单地跟随外部气氛。在 35,000 英尺的高度，外面的空气太稀薄，无法正常呼吸，这就是为什么加压舱保持在大约 6,000 至 8,000 英尺（1,800 至 2,400 米）的等效高度。温度也对方程式有帮助。 35,000 英尺高度的标准大气温度约为负 66°F（负 54°C），声速降至约 660 英里/小时（1,062 公里/小时），而海平面为 761 英里/小时（1,225 公里/小时）。仅供参考的机场指出，现代后掠翼喷气式飞机通常以 0.78 至 0.85 马赫的速度巡航，大约为 515 至 560 英里/小时（830 至 900 公里/小时）。据《军事与航空航天电子》报道，稀薄的空气可以减少阻力，让飞机燃烧的燃料能够飞行更远的距离。
这就是海拔的吸引力。但减少飞机周围的空气也会减少机翼和发动机可用的空气。最终，爬得更高不再是一种效率技巧，而是成为一个性能问题。
较高的海拔会减少阻力，但也会降低性能
稀薄的空气使邮轮变得经济实惠，但它也带来了下一个限制。机翼仍然必须产生足够的升力来支撑飞机，而升力部分取决于空气密度和空速的平方。在海平面密度约 31% 的情况下，客机必须在空中飞行得更快，或者以更高的迎角运行，才能产生承载相同重量所需的升力。军事与航空航天电子公司解释说，飞机可以通过速度和迎角进行补偿，但它不能无限期地保持爬升并期望性能保持不变。
发动机面临着自己的问题。正如您的里程可能会有所不同所指出的那样，在高海拔地区可用于燃烧的氧分子较少，从而降低了发动机推力。爬升本身也会消耗燃料，因此只有当巡航期间获得的效率超过到达目的地所花费的能量时，获得高度才值得。美国宇航局将巡航效率描述为飞机、发动机和操作条件的函数，而不是单一的理想高度。
该表还解释了为什么飞得更低并不是答案。在 10,000 英尺（3,048 米）的高度，喷气式飞机遇到的空气密度是 35,000 英尺高度的两倍多，这意味着空气动力阻力要大得多。它也更接近天气和其他交通。然而，最佳高度并不是固定的，因为飞机本身在整个飞行过程中会发生变化。
飞机重量使最佳巡航高度向上移动
一架长途飞机带着大量燃料离开登机口，并随着燃料的燃烧而逐渐变轻。这改变了它可以最有效运行的高度。军事和航空航天电子公司解释说，飞机的重量可能会降低飞行初期较高高度的效率，或者导致爬升时的性能裕度太小。美国宇航局同样将最佳巡航高度描述为与飞机重量密切相关。

AirportFYI 提供了一个说明性示例：一架从迪拜飞往伦敦的重载波音 777-300ER 可能会从 FL310 左右（即 31,000 英尺（9,449 米））的最佳高度开始，然后在几个小时后飞往 FL390（即 39,000 英尺（11,887 米））。飞机通常不会连续爬升。相反，工作人员可以进行分阶段的增加，称为阶梯攀登。 AirportFYI 表示，这些阶梯通常为 2,000 或 4,000 英尺（610 或 1,219 米），并引用行业研究估计，与保持在一个固定高度相比，在 12 至 16 小时的飞行中优化阶梯爬升可节省 1% 至 3% 的总燃油。
逐渐爬升反映了飞机重量的变化：随着燃料的燃烧，飞机变得更轻并且可以更有效地爬升。但即使是一架逐渐变轻的喷气式飞机最终也会达到一个点，飞得更高会带来一个新问题：安全高空飞行的两个边界开始相互靠近。
棺材角限制了客机高效巡航的高度
飞机爬升得越高，它在两个截然不同的空气动力学问题之间的空间就越小。第一个是飞得太慢并且接近失速。第二个是飞行速度太快，当机翼上的气流接近临界马赫时会遇到压缩效应。由于声速随着温度下降而下降，而在稀薄的空气中产生升力所需的真实空速则上升，因此这两个边界最终开始收敛。

summary: Brussels South Charleroi Airport says no flights will be able to take off or land between 07:00 and 21:00 on Monday, 23 November, after air navigation service provider skeyes informed it that air traffic control would be unavailable during the national demonst
summary_zh: 布鲁塞尔南沙勒罗瓦机场表示，11 月 23 日星期一 07:00 至 21:00 之间，空中导航后将无法起飞或降落任何航班
body_en: Charleroi warns of flight halt on 23 November as skeyes cannot provide ATC - Aviation24.be
Home Airports Brussels South Charleroi Airport (CRL) Charleroi warns of flight halt on 23 November as skeyes cannot provide...

Brussels South Charleroi Airport says no flights will be able to take off or land between 07:00 and 21:00 on Monday, 23 November, after air navigation service provider skeyes informed it that air traffic control would be unavailable during the national demonstration.
Passengers should avoid travelling to the airport without confirmation from their airline . Carriers will contact affected customers about rebooking, alternative travel or refunds.

BSCA said it had organised staffing to maintain operations on Monday, while respecting employees’ right to join the demonstration. The airport criticised the notice given by skeyes, saying the resulting disruption would affect thousands of passengers, airlines and the approximately 3,400 people working on the airport platform.

The airport also warned that repeated disruption damages confidence in Belgian aviation and called on the authorities to develop a coordinated plan to protect airport operations and competitiveness. BSCA teams remain mobilised to inform passengers and prepare for flights to resume once the restrictions end.
Source: Brussels South Charleroi Airport statement.

title_en: Influencer Uses AI To Score American First Class Upgrade… And Overpays
title_zh: 有影响力的人使用人工智能来获得美国头等舱升舱......并且支付过高
summary: An Instagram AI influencer says ChatGPT upgraded him to American first class. All it really did was book the instant upgrade price, when a systemwide upgrade was the smarter play.
summary_zh: 一位 Instagram 人工智能影响者表示 ChatGPT 将他升级为美国头等舱。它真正做的只是预订即时升级价格，当系统范围内
body_en: There’s no denying that AI holds a lot of potential to transform how we go about our every day life, both for better or worse.

People are increasingly using AI for travel planning, but here’s an interesting twist on that. Can AI help you find award flights and secure upgrades? It’s something I’d like to study in a bit more detail and write about in the coming weeks, but I just saw a post on Instagram that piqued my interest, so I figured it would make for a fun story. Consider this just a little teaser, for the time being.
“ChatGPT upgraded me to first class” — did it, though?

An Instagram user with 1.5 million followers who promises to help people master AI has just published a video about how “ChatGPT upgraded me to first class.” Now, that’s not as exciting as it sounds on the surface. The idea is simply that ChatGPT helped someone secure an upgrade through the standard means — it’s not like ChatGPT used his/her/their charm to sweet talk someone into an upgrade by dressing up nicely . 😉
Let me actually just quote the description of the video, which covers most of the content
What happens when you ask ChatGPT to upgrade your flight to first class?
I tried this on my flight in two weeks and it actually worked.
Go to ChatGPT and switch from Chat to Work at the top. Start a new chat and give it your airline and confirmation code.
“Ask me every question you need about my credit cards, my miles, and my memberships, and map out every upgrade currency I own for this exact flight.”
ChatGPT shows you that you’ve been sitting on upgrade power this whole time without even knowing it.
“Now look up my exact flight, check how empty the first class cabin is, and tell me every way I can get up there, ranked from free to cheapest.”
“Now go get me the upgrade. Use my miles if the math is worth it, and place the upgrade bid at the smartest number, or get me on the upgrade list right now.”
ChatGPT opens its own browser, logs into your airline, and actually chases that seat for you while you sit back and do nothing.
A post shared by Maverick Maltin | AI & ChatGPT (@mavgpt)
This isn’t the shining example that he thinks it is

I don’t want to suggest AI isn’t useful, but I’d say that the example given is actually very poor. First of all, let’s be clear about what’s actually going on here. He had booked a business class ticket on American from Los Angeles (LAX) to London (LHR), and then upgraded to first class.
Now, in the first place, something isn’t fully accurate here
He shows the first class boarding pass for November 26, 2026, which is five days from today, and boarding passes can be issued at most 24 hours out, so there must be some AI use there as well 😉

American actually eliminated first class as of November 19, 2026 , and stopped selling it for flights back in September 2026, so some part of this presumably isn’t true, if he claims that he did this two weeks before the flight

Okay, maybe he edited the dates, or something, which is fine, and it’s besides the point, but as a detail oriented airline nerd, I couldn’t help but notice those things. Anyway, let’s assume this is all accurate
body_zh: 不可否认，人工智能具有很大的潜力来改变我们的日常生活方式，无论是好是坏。
人们越来越多地使用人工智能进行旅行规划，但这里有一个有趣的变化。人工智能可以帮助您找到奖励航班并安全升舱吗？我想更详细地研究这个问题，并在接下来的几周内写下来，但我刚刚在 Instagram 上看到了一篇帖子，激起了我的兴趣，所以我认为这会是一个有趣的故事。暂时认为这只是一个小预告。
“ChatGPT 将我升级为头等舱”——是吗？
一位拥有 150 万粉丝、承诺帮助人们掌握人工智能的 Instagram 用户刚刚发布了一段视频，讲述“ChatGPT 如何将我升级为一流”。现在，这并不像表面上听起来那么令人兴奋。这个想法很简单，ChatGPT 帮助某人通过标准方式获得升级——ChatGPT 并不是利用他/她/他们的魅力，通过打扮得漂亮来甜言蜜语地说服某人升级。 😉
我其实只是引用视频的描述，它涵盖了大部分内容
当您要求 ChatGPT 将您的航班升级到头等舱时会发生什么？
两周后我在航班上尝试了这个方法，确实有效。
转到 ChatGPT 并从顶部的“聊天”切换到“工作”。开始新的聊天并向其提供您的航空公司和确认码。
“询问我有关我的信用卡、我的里程和我的会员资格的所有问题，并列出我为这次航班拥有的每种升舱货币。”
ChatGPT 向您展示，您一直在不知不觉中一直坐在升级电源上。
“现在查找我的确切航班，检查头等舱有多空，并告诉我到达那里的所有方式，从免费到最便宜的排名。”
“现在去给我升级。如果数学值得的话，使用我的里程，并将升级出价设置为最明智的数字，或者立即将我列入升级列表。”
ChatGPT 打开它自己的浏览器，登录您的航空公司，并在您坐下来什么也不做时实际上为您追逐那个座位。
Maverick Maltin 分享的帖子 |人工智能和 ChatGPT (@mavgpt)
这并不是他认为的光辉榜样
我并不是说人工智能没有用，但我想说的是，给出的例子实际上非常糟糕。首先，让我们弄清楚这里到底发生了什么。他预订了美国航空从洛杉矶（LAX）飞往伦敦（LHR）的商务舱机票，然后升级为头等舱。
首先，这里有些东西并不完全准确
他展示的是2026年11月26日的头等舱登机牌，距离今天还有五天，登机牌最多可以在24小时内发放，所以那里肯定也有一些AI的使用😉
美国航空实际上从 2026 年 11 月 19 日起取消了头等舱，并于 2026 年 9 月停止在航班上出售头等舱，因此，如果他声称自己在航班起飞前两周这样做了，那么这部分内容可能不属实。
好吧，也许他编辑了日期，或者其他什么，这很好，而且这不是重点，但作为一个注重细节的航空公司书呆子，我忍不住注意到这些事情。无论如何，我们假设这一切都是准确的

title_en: The Airlines Set To Replace Their Boeing 777s With New 777-9s Throughout The 2030s
title_zh: 航空公司计划在 2030 年代用新型 777-9 替换其波音 777
summary: Boeing has hundreds of 777-9 orders, but its first deliveries are years late. Here are the airlines waiting to replace their 777s.
summary_zh: 波音公司拥有数百架 777-9 订单，但其首次交付已经晚了好几年。以下是等待更换 777 飞机的航空公司。
body_en: Passionate about promoting aviation, the beauty of flight and the science behind it, Antonio is an avid reader of aviation magazines and books, and he loves visiting airshows all over the world, taking photos and writing about airplanes and helicopters as well. He is currently based in Palermo, Sicily.

Boeing has roughly 620 orders for an aircraft that has not delivered a single one yet, and some of the very first examples built may never reach the airline that paid for them. The 777-9 is meant to be the jet that carries the world's biggest long-haul airlines through the 2030s, but the program is about seven years behind its original 2020 service date, and the biggest customer has already turned away its first batch. For an industry that plans fleets decades ahead, that is a very awkward way to start a new era.

So who is really lining up to replace their Boeing 777s with the new 777-9, what exactly are they replacing, and when will passengers see the first one? The answers involve Emirates , Qatar Airways , Cathay Pacific , Singapore Airlines , and Lufthansa , plus a rival Airbus that has already started delivering.
Emirates & Qatar Airways Dominate The 777-9 Order Book

The scale of the commitment is hard to ignore. According to an order book compiled by Airways Magazine at the end of May 2026, the 777X program stood at 619 orders: 521 777-9s, 63 777-8 freighters, and 35 passenger 777-8s, all of them for Emirates. That is a remarkable number for an aircraft that has not carried a single paying passenger, and it makes the 777X Boeing's most important widebody bet of the decade. Airways also noted that the problem is certification, not demand, which is a rare thing to say about a program this delayed.

Emirates dominates the list. As reported by Emirates itself , its November 2025 Dubai Airshow deal added 65 more 777-9s, worth $38 billion at list prices, and lifted its total to 270 777Xs. The airline also holds options to convert part of that order into the 777-8 or the proposed, larger 777-10. Airways lists the split as 235 777-9s and 35 777-8s, so the exact mix is still fluid. Qatar Airways is second with 124 aircraft, made up of 90 777-9s and 34 777-8 freighters, followed by Cathay Pacific with 35 and Singapore Airlines with 31.

British Airways and its parent IAG have 24, Lufthansa Group has 27 (20 passenger jets and seven freighters), Korean Air has 20, and ANA has 20, including two freighters. Air India, Etihad, and Ethiopian Airlines hold 10, 10, and 8. But a long list of customers only tells us who wants the jet. It says nothing about what each of them plans to retire in exchange, or how long they will have to keep the old aircraft flying while they wait.
The Boeing 777-300ER Remains The Main Replacement Target

For most buyers, the answer is the Boeing 777-300ER, the best-selling long-haul widebody of its generation. Emirates alone flies 119 of them, plus 10 777-200LRs, according to its own fleet table. As noted by Simple Flying , the 777X is also pitched as a successor to high-capacity four-engine jets such as the Boeing 747 and the Airbus A380 , which burn far more fuel and cost more to maintain.

The new jet's biggest selling point is efficiency. According to Simple Flying's analysis of range and capacity , the 777-9 seats around 426 passengers against roughly 396 on a 777-300ER, while keeping a nearly identical range. The GE9X engines are expected to deliver up to 10% better fuel efficiency than the GE90-115B engines on the older jet.

The wing is the other trick: it spans 235 feet, 5 inches (71.8 meters) in flight, but its tips fold to 212 feet, 9 inches (64.9 meters) on the ground so it still fits standard gates. Boeing's pitch to airlines is simple: keep the long range, burn less fuel, and spend less on maintenance than the aging jets on the ramp.
Boeing 777-300ER vs. 777-9: the swap in numbers

On paper, that is a clean trade: more seats, similar range, lower fuel burn. The uncomfortable detail is that the older jets have to keep flying while the replacement is late, and that raises a very practical question about timing. Airways Magazine points out that carriers waiting on the 777-9 have had to stretch the lives of older 777-300ERs, A380s, and 747-400s, which adds maintenance, fuel, and cabin-product pressure with every extra year.
Lufthansa And Emirates Will Start The 777-9 Transition

Lufthansa will be the first, with Boeing targeting a 2027 delivery. Emirates said in November 2025 that it expects its first 777-9 from the second quarter of 2027, and its Boeing deliveries stretch all the way to 2038. That means the airline will be swapping 777-300ERs for 777-9s for more than a decade, which is exactly why this story belongs to the 2030s rather than to next year. Emirates still flies 116 Airbus A380s as well, so the transition will be gradual rather than a clean break.

Others will wait longer. According to Simple Flying , citing the Mainly Miles blog, Singapore Airlines' fleet plan shows no 777-9 deliveries in the 12 months to March 31, 2027, with Emirates, Qatar Airways, and Lufthansa ahead in the queue. That timing matters because Singapore Airlines is also planning a new premium economy product around the aircraft, making the 777-9 part of a future cabin strategy as well as a fleet replacement program.

Even the schedule itself is soft. Airways Magazine reported that FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford signaled the 777X would follow the 737 MAX 7 and MAX 10 into 2027 for certification. So queue position is one thing, but the airlines cannot simply take delivery because they are next in line. The more awkward problem is already sitting on Boeing's property: aircraft built years ago for customers that may no longer want them.
Early-Built 777-9s Are Now A Problem For Boeing

Between 2019 and 2021, Boeing built around 30 777-9s before the program stalled, including aircraft earmarked for Emirates and Lufthansa, according to German aviation outlet aero.de . By the time they could be delivered, they would be about eight years old and technically behind the final production standard. That creates an unusual problem for a brand-new aircraft: the earliest examples are already old enough to require substantial work before an airline wants them.

As reported by Simple Flying , Emirates rejected the first batch built for it because bringing those airframes up to the required standard would take extensive and costly rework. Boeing reportedly dismantled one early Emirates-bound 777-9 after the cost to fix it exceeded its value. Lufthansa has since said, on its second-quarter earnings call, that it will refuse some of its earliest aircraft, with Boeing contributing financially to upgrade the rest.
body_zh: 安东尼奥热衷于推广航空、飞行之美及其背后的科学，是航空杂志和书籍的狂热读者，他喜欢参观世界各地的航展，也喜欢拍摄有关飞机和直升机的照片和撰写有关飞机和直升机的文章。他目前居住在西西里岛巴勒莫。
波音公司大约有 620 份飞机订单，但尚未交付任何一架，而且首批制造的一些飞机可能永远不会到达付款的航空公司手中。 777-9 原本计划在 2030 年代成为世界上最大的长途航空公司的喷气式飞机，但该计划比原定的 2020 年服务日期晚了大约七年，而且最大的客户已经拒绝了第一批飞机。对于一个提前几十年规划车队的行业来说，这是开启新时代的一种非常尴尬的方式。
那么谁真正在排队用新的 777-9 替换他们的波音 777，他们到底要替换什么，乘客什么时候会看到第一架？答案包括阿联酋航空、卡塔尔航空、国泰航空、新加坡航空和汉莎航空，以及已经开始交付的竞争对手空中客车公司。
阿联酋航空和卡塔尔航空主导 777-9 订单
承诺的规模不容忽视。根据《航空杂志》2026 年 5 月底编制的一份订单簿，777X 项目共有 619 架订单：521 777-9、63 777-8 货机和 35 架 777-8 客机，全部为阿联酋航空。对于一架没有搭载任何付费乘客的飞机来说，这是一个了不起的数字，它使 777X 成为波音十年来最重要的宽体飞机赌注。航空公司还指出，问题在于认证，而不是需求，对于如此延迟的计划来说，这是很少见的。

阿联酋航空在榜单上占据主导地位。据阿联酋航空自己报道，其 2025 年 11 月迪拜航展交易增加了 65 架 777-9，按标价计算价值 380 亿美元，使其总数达到 270 777X。该航空公司还拥有将该订单的部分改装为 777-8 或拟议的更大 777-10 的选择权。航空公司将拆分列为 235 777-9 和 35 777-8，因此确切的组合仍然不稳定。卡塔尔航空位居第二，拥有 124 架飞机，其中包括 90 777-9 架飞机和 34 777-8 货机，其次是国泰航空（拥有 35 架飞机）和新加坡航空（拥有 31 架飞机）。
英国航空及其母公司 IAG 有 24 架，汉莎集团有 27 架（20 架客机和 7 架货机），大韩航空有 20 架，全日空有 20 架，其中包括两架货机。印度航空、阿提哈德航空和埃塞俄比亚航空分别拥有 10 架、10 架和 8 架。但一长串的客户名单只能告诉我们谁想要这架飞机。它没有说明他们每个人计划以什么退役作为交换，也没有说明他们在等待期间必须让旧飞机保持飞行多长时间。
波音 777-300ER 仍然是主要替代目标
对于大多数买家来说，答案是波音 777-300ER，这是同代中最畅销的长途宽体客机。根据阿联酋航空自己的机队表，仅阿联酋航空就有 119 架飞机，另外还有 10 架 777-200LR。正如《Simple Flying》指出的那样，777X 还被定位为大容量四引擎喷气式飞机（例如波音 747 和空客 A380）的后继者，后者燃烧的燃油更多，维护成本更高。
新飞机的最大卖点是效率。根据 Simple Flying 对航程和载客量的分析，777-9 可容纳约 426 名乘客，而 777-300ER 则可容纳约 396 名乘客，同时航程几乎相同。 GE9X 发动机预计比旧喷气机上的 GE90-115B 发动机的燃油效率提高 10%。
机翼是另一个技巧：它在飞行时跨度为 235 英尺 5 英寸（71.8 米），但其尖端在地面上折叠至 212 英尺 9 英寸（64.9 米），因此它仍然适合标准登机门。波音公司向航空公司提出的建议很简单：与停机坪上老化的喷气式飞机相比，保持长航程，燃烧更少的燃料，并减少维护费用。
波音 777-300ER 与 777-9：数字交换
从纸面上看，这是一个干净的交易：更多的座位、相似的航程、更低的燃油消耗。令人不安的细节是，旧飞机必须继续飞行，而更换飞机却迟到了，这就提出了一个非常实际的时间问题。 《航空杂志》指出，等待 777-9 的航空公司不得不延长旧型 777-300ER、A380 和 747-400 的使用寿命，这会逐年增加维护、燃油和客舱产品的压力。
汉莎航空和阿联酋航空将开始 777-9 过渡

汉莎航空将是第一家，波音公司的目标是 2027 年交付。阿联酋航空在 2025 年 11 月表示，预计从 2027 年第二季度开始交付第一架 777-9，而其波音交付量将一直持续到 2038 年。这意味着该航空公司将在十多年的时间内将 777-300ER 更换为 777-9，这也正是这个故事属于 2030 年代而不是明年的原因。阿联酋航空仍然拥有 116 架空客 A380 飞机，因此过渡将是渐进的，而不是彻底中断。
其他人会等待更长时间。据 Simple Flying 援引 Mainly Miles 博客报道，新加坡航空的机队计划显示，截至 2027 年 3 月 31 日的 12 个月内没有 777-9 交付，阿联酋航空、卡塔尔航空和汉莎航空排在前面。这个时机很重要，因为新加坡航空还计划围绕该飞机推出新的高端经济舱产品，使 777-9 成为未来客舱战略以及机队更换计划的一部分。
甚至日程本身也是软的。 《航空杂志》报道称，FAA 局长 Bryan Bedford 表示 777X 将跟随 737 MAX 7 和 MAX 10 进入 2027 年进行认证。因此，队列位置是一回事，但航空公司不能简单地接收货物，因为他们排在第二位。更尴尬的问题已经存在于波音公司的财产上：几年前为可能不再需要它们的客户制造的飞机。
早期制造的 777-9 现在对波音来说是一个问题
据德国航空媒体 aero.de 报道，2019 年至 2021 年间，波音公司在该计划陷入停滞之前建造了约 30 架 777-9，其中包括指定给阿联酋航空和汉莎航空的飞机。当它们交付时，它们已经有大约八年的历史，并且在技术上落后于最终的生产标准。这给一架全新的飞机带来了一个不寻常的问题：最早的飞机已经足够老了，需要进行大量工作才能被航空公司接受。
据 Simple Flying 报道，阿联酋航空拒绝了为其建造的第一批飞机，因为要使这些机身达到所需标准需要进行大量且成本高昂的返工。据报道，波音公司在修理成本超过其价值后拆解了一架早期飞往阿联酋航空的 777-9 飞机。此后，汉莎航空在第二季度财报电话会议上表示，将拒绝购买部分最早的飞机，而波音公司将出资升级其余飞机。

title_en: Avelo Airlines Cancels Massive 31 Routes: See Full List Now
title_zh: Avelo 航空公司大规模取消 31 条航线：立即查看完整列表
summary: Most are domestic.
summary_zh: 大部分都是国内的。
body_en: A graduate in German, Jake has a passion for history and regional aviation, and enjoys sampling new carriers and aircraft. He has visited OEM facilities as far and wide as Bristol, Toulouse, and Seattle, and recently enjoyed the milestone of flying his 150th sector as a passenger. Based in Norfolk, UK.

Avelo Airlines ' network for the winter 2026/27 season looks rather different to how it did in 2025/26. Most notably, 31 of the routes the carrier served this time last year are not being operated this time around, with 25 domestic and six international. Of the domestic cuts, a third are concentrated at one airport, highlighting the brutally competitive nature of the airline industry in the States.

On the international side, scheduling data from Cirium , an aviation analytics company, shows that all of the cuts impact short-haul services to key leisure markets in Mexico and the Caribbean. While the last year has seen Avelo make various route cuts, the airline is in flux, and it has a lot to look forward to fleet-wise with the Embraer E2 set to modernize its ops . The airline has ordered 50, with deliveries from 2028.

Wilmington International Airport (ILM) in North Carolina is a common factor when examining Avelo's winter network versus 12 months ago. Overall, the facility has lost winter service to nine destinations, four of which are in Florida: Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (FLL), Southwest Florida International Airport (RSW), Orlando International Airport (MCO), and West Palm Beach.

The remaining five route cuts concerned services from Wilmington to destinations in the northeast of the US. These included major hubs such as Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport (DTW) and Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD), as well as smaller destinations such as Islip, Manchester, and Rochester.
Avelo commented on its presence in Wilmington in a statement obtained earlier this year by Wilmington Biz .
"Wilmington is also not a protected airport. Most of the affected routes cannot handle more than one airline serving them due to demand."

While Wilmington has been the hardest-hit airport by Avelo's winter cuts, it is far from the only US facility to have lost routes. Elsewhere in North Carolina, the carrier is no longer serving five destinations from Raleigh-Durham International (RDU) that it did this time last year: these are Albany, Fort Myers, Grand Rapids, Manchester, and Rochester. Of course, the cuts extend beyond North Carolina.

For instance, Tweed New Haven Airport (HVN) has lost three winter Avelo Airlines routes: William P. Hobby Airport (HOU), Louis Armstrong International Airport (MSY), and Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD). Wilmington in Delaware (ILG) saw three cuts, namely to Jacksonville (JAX), Nashville (BNA), and Raleigh-Durham, while Nashville itself lost Rochester.

Returning to the state of North Carolina, Concord-Padgett Regional Airport (USA) no longer handles winter Avelo Airlines flights to West Palm Beach. Elsewhere, the American ultra-low-cost carrier also no longer flies from Islip to Lakeland Linder International Airport (LAL) in Florida in the winter. Still, it remains relatively busy, with 1,616 flights scheduled to operate this November. These will offer 300,784 seats.

On the international side, Wilmington International Airport has also lost winter Avelo Airlines flights to Punta Cana International Airport (PUJ) in the Dominican Republic. The carrier has also ceased its winter services to this popular Caribbean leisure destination from Bradley International Airport (BDL) in Windsor Locks, Connecticut, and Raleigh-Durham International Airport (RDU).

Windsor Locks has also lost winter Avelo Airlines flights to Cancún International Airport (CUN) in Mexico, and the carrier has ceased winter service from both Windsor Locks and Raleigh-Durham to Sangster International Airport (MBJ) in Montego Bay, Jamaica. The cessation of these routes marked the end of Avelo Airlines' international flights , which had only commenced operations back in 2024 .

body_zh: 杰克毕业于德语，对历史和支线航空充满热情，并喜欢尝试新的航母和飞机。他参观过远至布里斯托尔、图卢兹和西雅图的 OEM 工厂，最近还享受了作为乘客飞行第 150 个航段的里程碑。总部位于英国诺福克。
阿维洛航空公司 2026/27 年冬季的网络看起来与 2025/26 年有很大不同。最值得注意的是，该航空公司去年此时运营的航线中有 31 条今年不再运营，其中 25 条是国内航线，6 条是国际航线。在国内裁员中，三分之一集中在一个机场，凸显了美国航空业的残酷竞争本质。
在国际方面，航空分析公司 Cirium 的调度数据显示，所有削减都影响了墨西哥和加勒比地区主要休闲市场的短途服务。尽管去年阿维罗航空公司进行了各种航线削减，但该航空公司仍在不断变化，随着巴西航空工业公司 E2 飞机将使其运营现代化，该公司在机队方面有很多值得期待的地方。该航空公司已订购 50 架，将于 2028 年开始交付。
与 12 个月前相比，在检查 Avelo 的冬季网络时，北卡罗来纳州威尔明顿国际机场 (ILM) 是一个常见因素。总体而言，该机场已停止飞往九个目的地的冬季航班，其中四个位于佛罗里达州：劳德代尔堡好莱坞国际机场 (FLL)、西南佛罗里达国际机场 (RSW)、奥兰多国际机场 (MCO) 和西棕榈滩。
其余 5 条航线削减了从威尔明顿飞往美国东北部目的地的相关服务。其中包括底特律大都会韦恩县机场 (DTW) 和华盛顿杜勒斯国际机场 (IAD) 等主要枢纽，以及艾斯利普、曼彻斯特和罗切斯特等较小的目的地。
Avelo 在 Wilmington Biz 今年早些时候获得的一份声明中对其在威尔明顿的业务发表了评论。
“威尔明顿也不是一个受保护的机场。由于需求，大多数受影响的航线无法容纳多家航空公司提供服务。”
虽然威尔明顿机场是受阿维洛冬季削减影响最严重的机场，但它并不是美国唯一一个失去航线的机场。在北卡罗来纳州的其他地方，该航空公司不再像去年这个时候那样为罗利-达勒姆国际机场 (RDU) 的五个目的地提供服务：奥尔巴尼、迈尔斯堡、大急流城、曼彻斯特和罗切斯特。当然，削减范围超出了北卡罗来纳州。
例如，特威德纽黑文机场 (HVN) 失去了 Avelo Airlines 的 3 条冬季航线：威廉·霍比机场 (HOU)、路易斯·阿姆斯特朗国际机场 (MSY) 和华盛顿杜勒斯国际机场 (IAD)。特拉华州威尔明顿 (ILG) 被淘汰了 3 次，分别是杰克逊维尔 (JAX)、纳什维尔 (BNA) 和罗利-达勒姆，而纳什维尔本身则失去了罗切斯特。
回到北卡罗来纳州，康科德-帕吉特地区机场（美国）不再执飞 Avelo 航空公司飞往西棕榈滩的冬季航班。在其他地方，这家美国超低成本航空公司也不再在冬季从艾斯利普飞往佛罗里达州莱克兰林德国际机场 (LAL) 的航班。尽管如此，它仍然相对繁忙，今年 11 月计划运营 1,616 个航班。这些将提供 300,784 个座位。
在国际方面，威尔明顿国际机场也失去了阿维洛航空公司飞往多米尼加共和国蓬塔卡纳国际机场（PUJ）的冬季航班。该航空公司还停止了从康涅狄格州温莎洛克斯布拉德利国际机场 (BDL) 和罗利达勒姆国际机场 (RDU) 飞往这个受欢迎的加勒比休闲目的地的冬季航班。
温莎洛克斯还失去了阿维洛航空公司飞往墨西哥坎昆国际机场 (CUN) 的冬季航班，该航空公司还停止了从温莎洛克斯和罗利达勒姆飞往牙买加蒙特哥湾桑斯特国际机场 (MBJ) 的冬季航班。这些航线的终止标志着 Avelo Airlines 国际航班的结束，该航班于 2024 年才开始运营。
